title: Bimodal session stress-surface simulator for continuous-batch queueing effects
creator: Alexei Morozov
description: Goal: build a reproducible simulator and analysis pipeline that quantifies how continuous batching + request queueing amplifies tail latency and depresses tokens/sec under mixed (bimodal) session profiles. This ticket captures design, implementation, and validation of a stress-surface generator that produces arrival traces, exercises the serving runtime, and produces deterministic regression signals (EWMA/CUSUM) for p95 and tokens/sec. Results will inform autoscaling and batching defaults for mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic arrival generator that can produce bimodal session mixes (short chat-like sessions and long document sessions) with configurable proportions, inter-arrival distributions, and warm KV cache fractions

End-to-end harness that submits traces to the runtime (hosted/dedicated local test cluster) and captures detailed timing: client queue time, server queue time, batch formation time, per-token service time, and final latency percentiles

Automated analysis pipeline that computes tokens/sec and p95 time series, applies EWMA and CUSUM detectors, and emits a regression boolean with a documented delta threshold (default: 10% p95 degradation or 15% drop in tokens/sec) and significance level
Grafana dashboard with an experiment surface: x-axis = fraction of long sessions, y-axis = offered load (rps), heatmaps for p95 and tokens/sec, and an annotation layer for when detectors fired
Reproducible experiment spec files (seeded) and a sample report comparing current runtime-1.22 vs baseline runtime-1.20 with clear artifacts (CSV + plots) stored in S3
Unit/integration tests for the arrival generator and analyzer with >=80% deterministic coverage for edge cases (pure-short, pure-long, 50/50 mix, high burstiness)
PR with code + instructions + runbook merged and documented in Confluence link referenced in artifacts
tasks: (Design) Write experiment spec: session classes, length distributions, arrival process families, cache-hit model, and GPU profiles
(Impl) Implement bimodal arrival generator with configurable distributions (Poisson, Pareto burstiness, time-varying load) and deterministic seeding
(Impl) Extend local load runner to capture queue/batch formation metrics (client enqueue time, batch cut time, server-dequeue time)
(Impl) Add lightweight model stub harness to emulate KV-cache hit latency vs miss paths for long sessions
(Analysis) Implement EWMA and CUSUM detectors and a bootstrap significance test for p95 shifts
(Infra) S3 artifact writer and experiment metadata manifest + storage conventions
(Dash) Create Grafana dashboard panels and an automated job to publish heatmaps after each experiment run
(Validation) Run smoke experiments at 25%, 50%, 100% target loads across short/long mixes and record deterministic seedable outputs
(Docs) Confluence runbook and README with reproduction steps and recommended runtime knob adjustments
(Cleanup) Add tests, fix flaky timing measurement, and address PR feedback
test_matrix: Session classes: short (8-64 tokens), medium (256-1024), long (1024-4096). Mix ratios: 100% short, 80/20, 50/50, 20/80, 100% long. Arrival patterns: Poisson, bursty-Pareto (alpha=1.5), diurnal sinusoidal. Offered load sweep: 0.1x to 1.6x average capacity in steps. Hardware profiles: a2-standard (single-GPU), p4d-sim, quantized int8 runtime. KV cache hit fractions: 0%, 30%, 70%, 95%. Concurrency: 16, 64, 256 sessions. Seeded RNG used for reproducibility.
analysis_pipeline: 1) Ingest JSON line logs from load runner and runtime metrics (prometheus) into S3 staging. 2) Time-align events per request id and compute per-request breakdown. 3) Aggregate into fixed-width time windows (30s) to produce rolling tokens/sec and latency percentiles. 4) Apply EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.2) and run CUSUM with configurable thresholds; flag windows that exceed delta thresholds. 5) Bootstrap p95 samples across independent seeds for confidence intervals. 6) Emit experiment manifest, CSVs, and pre-rendered heatmap PNGs. 7) Post results to Grafana snapshot and link in artifacts.
notes: We intentionally model long sessions with progressive KV-cache growth so early tokens behave like short sessions and later tokens exercise full decode costs.
Detector thresholds are conservative for initial runs to avoid false positives due to burstiness; we'll tighten after 5-10 repeated seeds.
Risk: measuring precise batch formation time requires hooks in the serving runtime that may add overhead; implement opt-in instrumentation flags.
Tradeoff: deterministic seeding reduces realism of diurnal patterns; we will add 'pseudo-random seeds' later for stress testing non-deterministic regression sensitivity.
